about: The prayer before the priest receives the Precious Blood joins Psalm 115:3–4 to Psalm 17:4 in the Vulgate numbering. The first verse accompanies the gathering of fragments and the wiping of the paten over the chalice. The priest then takes the chalice and says the remaining verses. “Salutáris” is a noun here: “the chalice of salvation”.

seg.nr: The priest uncovers the chalice, genuflects, gathers any fragments and wipes the paten clean over the chalice, saying meanwhile:

seg.tr: What shall I give back to the Lord for all He has given me?

fn.w001: Neuter accusative, serving as the object of “retríbuam” (w002).
fn.w002: This edition parses the form as a deliberative subjunctive: the psalmist asks what he is to render to the Lord. The same form can be future indicative. The received translation retains the natural “What shall I render?”
fn.w006: Object of “retríbuit” (w007), not its subject: the things He rendered.
fn.w007: The present and perfect have the same form here. The context indicates the perfect: “He has rendered”.
fn.w008: “retríbuam” (w002) and “retríbuit” (w007) are forms of the same verb: what I shall render to the Lord and what He has rendered to me.

nt.w002: The ending -am is future indicative and present subjunctive at once. What shall I render, or what am I to render — a deliberative question. This edition takes the subjunctive and marks the doubt.

seg.tr: I will take the chalice of salvation and call upon the name of the Lord.

fn.w010: Genitive of the neuter noun “salutáre”: “the chalice of salvation”.
fn.w011: Future indicative, as at the Host: “invocábo” (w015) beside it can only be future.

seg.tr: I will call upon the Lord with praise, and I will be saved from my enemies.

fn.w016: A participle used adverbially: “praising, I will call upon the Lord”.
fn.w023: With “ero” (w024), it forms a future predicate: “I shall be safe”.

seg.nr: The priest takes the chalice in his right hand and signs himself with it, saying:

seg.tr: May the Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ preserve my soul for eternal life. Amen.

fn.w025: The formula parallels the prayer before receiving the Host. “Corpus” is replaced here by “Sanguis”.

seg.nr: Holding the paten beneath the chalice with his left hand, the priest reverently consumes all the Blood together with the particle.
